## Corrupt or truncated landing files
Symptom: `ingest` fails with `failed loading raw.<table> from <table>.csv:` followed by a CSV parse error (unterminated quoted value, wrong number of columns, unexpected end of file).

- Open the file: check the size, last lines, and whether the final row is cut off.
- Compare the header to the contract. If the header is fine and the tail is cut off, the export was interrupted.
- This is a one-off delivery glitch. Use `request_upstream_redelivery` for the day with the affected tables, then rerun.
- Do not edit the CSV by hand or truncate it to the last good row: a partial file means missing rows.
- If redelivery produces the same broken file, escalate to `upstream_app_team`.

## Choosing quickly
| Finding | Action |
|---|---|
| landing file missing / row drop (partial or filtered) | `request_upstream_redelivery` (orders, order_items, payments) |
| corrupt or truncated file | `request_upstream_redelivery` |
| duplicates within one file | `deduplicate_on_ingest` or redelivery |
| stale rows from a previous day | `request_upstream_redelivery` |
| renamed column | `apply_column_mapping` |
| `$`-formatted amounts | `set_column_parser` (`strip_currency`) |
| new non-contract column | `ignore_extra_columns` |
| required column dropped, no source | `escalate_to_owner` (`upstream_app_team`) |
| changed dbt model broke build or numbers | `revert_model_change` |
| transient, cause cleared | `rerun_only` |
| nothing safe applies | `escalate_to_owner` |

## Remedy for one-off export glitches
- Use `request_upstream_redelivery` for the day with ALL affected related tables together: `orders`, `order_items`, and `payments` (add `customers` only if it is also affected).
- Redelivery re-runs the export and produces a correct file for each table.
- Redelivering just `orders` when items/payments were also cut leaves referential mismatches.
- Then rerun the partition and verify.

## Symptoms
- `ingest` fails: `landing file missing: landing/<table>/dt=<date>/<table>.csv` (loud).
- Check `partition_present:raw.<table>` fails: `raw.<table> partition <date> has 0 rows` (silent: an empty file loads fine).
- Check `row_count_trend:raw.<table>` fails: today's rows fall outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median.
- Check `reconciliation:raw.orders->marts.fct_orders` fails: distinct raw orders for the day differ from `fct_orders` rows.
- Check `freshness:marts.fct_orders` fails: latest order date in the mart is behind the partition.
- Business symptom: revenue or order count for a day looks too low.

| corrupt or truncated file | `request_upstream_redelivery` |

## Remedy for one-off export glitches
- Use `request_upstream_redelivery` for the day with ALL affected related tables together: `orders`, `order_items`, and `payments` (add `customers` only if it is also affected).
- Redelivery re-runs the export and produces a correct file for each table.
- Redelivering just `orders` when items/payments were also cut leaves referential mismatches.
- Then rerun the partition and verify.

## Why asking upstream to resend does NOT fix this
- Renames, new columns, drops and reformatting are deliberate, persistent upstream changes applied to every export from an effective day onward.
- A redelivery re-runs the export and reproduces the same changed file, with the same header and formats.
- `request_upstream_redelivery` is for one-off export glitches only (missing, truncated, duplicated files).
- If the change is wrong from upstream's point of view, that is a conversation with `upstream_app_team`, not a resend.

findings.claim: Symptoms of a missing file: ingest fails loudly with `landing file missing: landing/<table>/dt=<date>/<table>.csv`. An empty file loads silently, and shows up as a failing `partition_present` check (0 rows), a `row_count_trend` outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median, or a reconciliation or freshness failure on fct_orders.

The remediation table maps 'landing file missing / row drop (partial or filtered)' to `request_upstream_redelivery` for orders, order_items and payments. Corrupt or truncated files and stale rows from a previous day get the same action.

Request redelivery for the day with ALL affected related tables together (orders, order_items, payments, plus customers only if it is also affected). Redelivering only orders when items or payments were also cut leaves referential mismatches. Then rerun the partition and verify.
For truncated files, do not hand-edit the CSV or cut it to the last good row, because a partial file means missing rows. If redelivery returns the same broken file, escalate to `upstream_app_team`.

Do not request redelivery for renamed, added or dropped columns or reformatted values. These are persistent upstream changes, so a resend reproduces the same file. `request_upstream_redelivery` is only for one-off glitches (missing, truncated, duplicated files). Use `apply_column_mapping`, `set_column_parser`, `ignore_extra_columns` or `escalate_to_owner` instead.
`rerun_only` applies only when the failure was transient and its cause has cleared. `escalate_to_owner` applies when nothing safe applies.
